1

  • N: ludlul | bēl nēmeqi || ila | muštāla
  • T: I will praise the lord of wisdom, solicitous god,
  • L: ludlul ← dalālu II “to praise”; bēl ← bēlu I “lord”; nēmeqi ← nēmequ I “wisdom, sagacity Bab., M/NA civilising knowledge”; ila ← ilu I “pl. ilū, ilānu god, deity a or the god, also du.”; muštāla ← muštālu I “who considers”
  • Note: See [fromebllab0028: 140]: "This is the only MS that uses the plural writing DINGIR-MEŠ for the singular ila in I 1 and I 3 (compare the description "repeated ilāni muštalu … uri" for this fragment in [RN3551: 469]). For the use of the plural marker as a way to indicate that the preceding sign should be read logographically, see [RN1428: 282-287]."

  • N: īnuššu | ina karašê || ušatbi | maqta
  • T: At the cast of his glance, he raises the fallen from annihilation.
  • L: īnuššu ← ênu I, -šu I “to look askance m/jB”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; karašê ← karāšu II “catastrophe, disaster O/jB”; ušatbi ← tebû I “OAkk, Ass. tabā'u(m), NB tabû to get up, arise, set out”; maqta ← maqtu I “fallen Bab., NA”
  • Note: As opposed to the interpretation inūšu, “at that time, then”, īnuššu is here understood as derived from the verb ênu, “to eye” (see [RN3205: 276] with the reference to [RN355aa: 29-30]).

The suggested correction muš-mid!-di in [RN2254: 184] (the text having MAN instead of BE as a result of scribal error) would consequently be unnecessary. Still, this does not help in identifying the following noun that has been assumed to be rihiṣti. The collation of KalNA1 confirms that there are traces of two signs before the sequence with TI, AN and IM. This rules out the possibility of having a logographic writing for rihiṣti adad, which in itself would be unusual in an overwhelmingly syllabically written poem.

  • Note: The form zammāru is preferred here over the variant zammāriš in KalNA1. [RN2709: 536] cites zammāru in this line as evidence for a comparative -um, but a more plausible interpretation is that it is a predicative complement.
